headline: Alphabet's call puts a number on AI capex as the memory squeeze reaches phones

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: It's ten to three UTC on Friday, October thirtieth. This is Aradio. The money behind AI got a little clearer this hour, and the memory shortage reached your phone.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Alphabet's earnings call was the lead. The company raised its full-year capital spending outlook again, and almost all of the increase is servers and data centres for AI.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: The question investors keep asking is whether any of that spending is earning money yet. Sundar Pichai had an answer ready.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On the call he said cloud backlog grew faster than capital expenditure this quarter, and called that the clearest signal the demand is real. That is a claim about contracts signed, not revenue booked, so it is worth holding him to it next quarter.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Microsoft reports on Wednesday. Analysts expect another raise in its spending guidance, and Azure growth is the number to watch.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: Now the other side of that spending. High-bandwidth memory for AI chips is sold out through next year at all three suppliers, and the squeeze is spreading.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Today a phone maker blamed a gross-margin miss on memory prices. Its chief financial officer said memory is the single biggest headwind this quarter and won't ease before the second half of next year.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: That is the first consumer company to say it out loud. We have moved that story to escalating.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: Samsung's call on Thursday is the next test. If its memory guidance rises again, expect more of those warnings.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: On Anthropic's IPO, two reports now point to a confidential filing before the end of the year. The company declined to comment, so treat the timing as reported, not confirmed.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: And on the EU's code of practice for general-purpose models, nothing new signed this week. The AI Office published its first supervisory priorities; that story is steady.

lines.speaker: Speaker 2
lines.text: What to watch: Microsoft on Wednesday, Samsung on Thursday, and any confirmation of an Anthropic filing.

lines.speaker: Speaker 1
lines.text: That's Aradio. We'll be back when the picture changes.
